findings.title: provider quotas supplied through OS environment variables (Spring relaxed binding) are silently dropped; with unconfigured=unlimited every provider ends up unlimited
findings.evidence: docs/execution/reviews/T08-round3/evidence/r3cfg-out.txt probes 7a/7b/7c (java exit 0): getProperty('editorial.cost.provider-quota.mock.max-concurrent') = 2 while BudgetPolicyConfig.from(env) yields providers={} unconfigured=UNLIMITED; with refuse it is REFUSE providers={}
findings.judgement: BudgetPolicyConfig.java:90-94 enumerates raw property names and requires the dotted prefix, while BudgetPolicyConfig.java:78/:156-160 reads the switch through env.getProperty (relaxed binding). Same failure class as round-2 F2-01 (configured correctly, silently never applies) in a different channel.
findings.reachability: infra/compose.yml sets no EDITORIAL_COST_* variables and application.yml:78 only carries the feature gate, so this is a deployment-shaped trap, not a live defect.
findings.requiredFix: loud rejection when EDITORIAL_COST_PROVIDER_QUOTA_* shaped keys exist but no quota entry was enumerated, or a stated activation precondition plus a test; a reverse control for either.

findings.title: the nested-YAML binding proof is removable without turning any gate or any test red
findings.evidence: docs/execution/reviews/T08-round3/evidence/gate_probe.json: A1 (loader moved into an uncalled helper, yaml() hand-builds flat keys, nested text kept in the body) => check 11 GREEN; B1 (live case serves from(env) then overrides with a hand-built policy) => checks 11 and 14 GREEN; A2 (nested document moved out of the body) => RED, so only the body-scoped shape scan is load-bearing. docs/execution/reviews/T08-round3/evidence/variant-report.json V6 = compilable B1 run on the live cluster: 49/49 GREEN.
findings.judgement: verify.py:498-499 tests file-wide substrings ('the word appeared in the file'), verify.py:505-506 is the only body-scoped test; nothing follows the data flow from the loader into the policy the case asserts on.
findings.requiredFix: scope the loader/ByteArrayResource/from(env) evidence to java_method_body of the two cases, add a rule that the case body calls service() exactly once, and make the fixture numbers unreachable by any hand-built policy in the file.

findings.title: layering resolves to override, so a looser model entry lifts the provider-wide ceiling; no case distinguishes override from overlay
findings.evidence: variant-report.json P1 (implementation untouched, only two reviewer cases added; exit 0, T08PostgresTest 33/0/0): provider max-concurrent=2 with mock-gpt max-concurrent=5 admits 3 live holds on mock-gpt. variant-report.json V1 (enforce both levels, i.e. stricter) => 49/49 GREEN.
findings.judgement: BudgetPolicy.java:112-117 prefers the exact scope, BudgetService.java:295-307 measures only that entry's window; CostPricingTest.java:368-373 asserts the override preference at map level, so the design is intentional but unratified and the service path has no case for the looser-override direction.
findings.requiredFix: pick one semantics and pin it: either overlay (check both windows) plus a service-path case, or reject at assembly time a model leaf looser than the same provider's leaf; state the choice in the activation preconditions for Owner sign-off.

findings.title: dot-in-model-id (ledger T08-R3-DOTMODEL) adjudication
findings.evidence: r3cfg-out.txt 3a/3b (model-level quota for 'gpt-4.1' -> 503 INVALID_PROVIDER_QUOTA_KEY in both nested YAML and flat writings), 4/4b (quotaScope('mock','gpt-4.1') = 'mock', perModel=false, quota present; unlisted provider = null), variant-report.json P1 reviewerDottedModelIdUsesTheProviderWindow (live cluster: two admits, third refused PROVIDER_QUOTA_EXCEEDED with a provider-wide ceiling of 2)
findings.judgement: (a) model-level quotas are not configurable for dotted model ids - loudly, at assembly, in both config writings; no silent entry loss. (b) with a provider-level entry the runtime metering for dotted model ids is correct - the request answers the provider scope so its rows land in the provider window. (c) capability gap, not a defect; P3.
findings.ownership: reviewer ruled loud-vs-silent only; the config-shape choice belongs to the main agent (integration surface) - recommended provider-quota.entries[] list form, escaping rejected because a second spelling is exactly the F2-01 disease; whether dotted product models need per-model ceilings belongs to the Owner (OQ-09 is due before real API tests, where gpt-4.1 / claude-3.5-sonnet appear).
findings.requiredFix: either the entries[] shape with cases, or an activation precondition stating that dotted model ids can only carry provider-level quotas.

findings.title: the separator is not excluded from provider/model ids, so two scopes collide and leaves overwrite each other
findings.evidence: r3cfg-out.txt 9a/9b: configuring provider-quota.p|q.* (9/9) together with provider-quota.p.q.* (1/1) yields {p|q=ProviderQuota[maxConcurrent=9, callsPerDay=1]} and providerQuota('p','q') returns that hybrid
findings.judgement: BudgetPolicy.scope():44-47 does not validate segments; the constructor (:86-90) rejects dots and leading/trailing pipes only; BudgetService.java:69-70 and V5 (varchar(64)/varchar(128)) impose no character rules on provider/model.
findings.requiredFix: refuse a provider or model segment containing '|' (and '.', already refused as a key) with 503 INVALID_PROVIDER_QUOTA_KEY, plus a case.

findings.title: check 11 overstates its coverage and fires on benign equivalent rewrites
findings.evidence: gate_probe.json: F1 (perModel via indexOf instead of contains, same predicate) RED; F4 (binding split into a local variable) RED; F2 (line wrap) GREEN; F3 (javadoc re-worded) GREEN. join_probe.json: J3 (a second provider+"|"+model join added inside CostLedger.java, quotaScope call kept) GREEN - verify.py:467 builds the joined scan from policy + config only; J1/J2 go RED only because they also delete policy.quotaScope(provider, model) and trip wide_window.
findings.judgement: docs/execution/reports/T08.md:46 claims the check asserts a single join for the whole module; verify.py:467 builds that scan from `policy + config` only, i.e. two of nineteen files. Conversely, two legal refactors (indexOf for contains, an added local variable) turn the build gate red.
findings.requiredFix: widen the join scan to the cost module or re-word the claim; relax the perModel and service() anchors to semantic shapes so equivalent rewrites stay green, and add a benign-probe reverse control pair.
